claim: Muscle cells of syndapin III KO mice show severe reductions of caveolae reminiscent of human caveolinopathies.
source: We show that muscle cells of syndapin III KO mice show severe reductions of caveolae reminiscent of human caveolinopathies.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by electron microscopy data presented in the manuscript showing reduced caveolae density in syndapin III KO muscle cells.

claim: The levels of plasma membrane-associated caveolar coat proteins caveolin3 and cavin1 were both not reduced upon syndapin III KO.
source: Yet, different from other mouse models, the levels of the plasma membrane-associated caveolar coat proteins caveolin3 and cavin1 were both not reduced upon syndapin III KO.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative western blot analyses and immunogold labeling data showing unchanged caveolin3 and CAVIN-1 levels at the plasma membrane in syndapin III KO cells.

claim: Neither caveolin3 nor caveolin3 and cavin1 together are sufficient to form caveolae.
source: This allowed for dissecting bona fide caveolar functions from those supported by mere caveolin presence and also demonstrated that neither caveolin3 nor caveolin3 and cavin1 are sufficient to form caveolae.
evidence: The manuscript demonstrates through electron microscopy that despite the presence of caveolin3 and CAVIN-1 at the plasma membrane in syndapin III KO cells, caveolar invaginations are severely impaired.

claim: Syndapin III is crucial for caveolar invagination.
source: The membrane-shaping protein syndapin III is crucial for caveolar invagination and KO rendered the cells sensitive to membrane tensions.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing severe reduction of caveolar invaginations in syndapin III KO cells, combined with the presence of syndapin III at caveolar necks in wild-type cells.

claim: Syndapin III KO rendered cells sensitive to membrane tensions.
source: The membrane-shaping protein syndapin III is crucial for caveolar invagination and KO rendered the cells sensitive to membrane tensions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by Trypan Blue assays showing increased cell rupture in syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes under hypoosmotic stress conditions.

claim: The physiological role of caveolae is to counterpoise membrane tensions.
source: Consistent with this physiological role of caveolae in counterpoising membrane tensions, syndapin III KO skeletal muscles showed pathological parameters upon physical exercise that are also found in CAVEOLIN3 mutation-associated muscle diseases.
evidence: This is supported by data showing caveolar flattening under hypoosmotic stress and pathological changes in syndapin III KO muscles after exercise.

claim: Syndapin III KO skeletal muscles showed pathological parameters upon physical exercise that are also found in CAVEOLIN3 mutation-associated muscle diseases.
source: Consistent with this physiological role of caveolae in counterpoising membrane tensions, syndapin III KO skeletal muscles showed pathological parameters upon physical exercise that are also found in CAVEOLIN3 mutation-associated muscle diseases.
evidence: This is demonstrated by histological analyses showing detached nuclei, necrosis, and inflammation in trained syndapin III KO muscles.

claim: Caveolae were first described more than 60 years ago.
source: Caveolae - uniform plasma membrane invaginations with ~70 nm diameter - were first described more than 60 years ago (Yamada, 1955).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by citation to Yamada, 1955.

claim: Caveolae are uniform plasma membrane invaginations with ~70 nm diameter.
source: Caveolae - uniform plasma membrane invaginations with ~70 nm diameter - were first described more than 60 years ago (Yamada, 1955).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation and confirmed by electron microscopy measurements in this study.

claim: Caveolin3 is a main structural component of caveolar coats in muscles.
source: A main structural component of caveolar coats in muscles is caveolin3 (cav3).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by immunolabeling data showing caveolin3 at caveolae in muscle cells.

claim: CAV3 mutations manifest in several human diseases including limb girdle muscular dystrophy, rippling muscle disease, hyperCKemia, distal myopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic-long-QT syndrome and sudden-infant-death syndrome.
source: CAV3 mutations manifest in several human diseases, for example limb girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD), rippling muscle disease (RMD), hyperCK(creatine kinase)emia, distal myopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic-long-QT syndrome and sudden-infant-death syndrome.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation to Gazzerro et al., 2010.

claim: Most patients with CAV3 mutations are heterozygous and the pathophysiology seems to be caused by the mutated protein acting dominant-negatively on WT-cav3 via self-association.
source: Most patients with CAV3 mutations are heterozygous and the pathophysiology seems to be caused by the mutated protein acting dominant-negatively on WT-cav3 via self-association (Gazzerro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gazzerro et al., 2010.

claim: Overexpression of dominant-negative cav3 mutants in mice caused symptoms resembling hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
source: Consistently, also overexpression of dominant-negative mutants in mice caused symptoms resembling hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (Ohsawa et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ohsawa et al., 2004.

claim: Cav3 KO led to a lack of caveolae, size variability of muscle fibers and cases of necrosis considered as signs of muscle dystrophy.
source: Cav3 KO led to a lack of caveolae, size variability of muscle fibers and cases of necrosis considered as signs of muscle dystrophy (Hagiwara et al., 2000; Galbiati et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hagiwara et al., 2000 and Galbiati et al., 2001.

claim: Cav3 KO hearts were unaltered in one study.
source: Cav3 KO hearts were unaltered in one study (Galbiati et al., 2001), whereas another reported heart hypertrophy and dilation (Woodman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Galbiati et al., 2001.

claim: Another study reported heart hypertrophy and dilation in cav3 KO mice.
source: Cav3 KO hearts were unaltered in one study (Galbiati et al., 2001), whereas another reported heart hypertrophy and dilation (Woodman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Woodman et al., 2002.

claim: In zebrafish, cav3 knock-down caused notochord and myoblast fusion defects and impaired movement.
source: In zebrafish, cav3 knock-down caused notochord and myoblast fusion defects and impaired movement (Nixon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nixon et al., 2005.

claim: Patients with heterozygous V57M CAV3 mutation showed hyperCKemia, yet cav3 levels only were reduced by 62%.
source: Patients with heterozygous V57M exchange showed hyperCKemia, yet, cav3 levels only were reduced by 62% (Alias et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Alias et al., 2004.

claim: The heterozygous disease mutations CAV3 P28L and R27E did not lead to any significant reduction in caveolae density in quantitative electron microscopical analyses of patient biopsies.
source: The heterozygous disease mutations CAV3 P28L and R27E did not lead to any significant reduction in caveolae density in quantitative electron microscopical analyses of patient biopsies (Timmel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Timmel et al., 2015.

claim: In LGMD-1C patients with the severest cases of CAV3 missense mutations known (63TFT65del and P104L), caveolae formation was not fully abolished but 7 or 24% of WT remained.
source: Even in LGMD-1C patients with the severest cases of CAV3 missense mutations known (63TFT65del and P104L) showing full clinical symptoms, caveolae formation was not fully abolished but 7 or 24% of WT remained, as judged from the representative images presented (Minetti et al., 1998; Minetti et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Minetti et al., 1998 and Minetti et al., 2002.

claim: The same CAV3 mutation can lead to different clinical phenotypes.
source: Furthermore, the observation that the same CAV3 mutation can lead to different clinical phenotypes suggests additional, maybe indirect mechanisms (Fischer et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fischer et al., 2003.

claim: Major portions of both endogenous non-muscle caveolins, cav1 and cav2, were not located at deeply invaginated classical caveolar profiles.
source: Extensive quantitative analyses demonstrated that major portions of both of the endogenous non-muscle caveolins, cav1 and cav2, were not located at deeply invaginated classical caveolar profiles (Fujimoto et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fujimoto et al., 2000.

claim: Cav1-caveolar invaginations were highlighted as membrane tension buffers.
source: Apart from such putatively distinct functions of caveolin, cav1-caveolar invaginations were highlighted as membrane tension buffers in a recent seminal paper (Sinha et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sinha et al., 2011.

claim: CAVIN-1 KO phenotypically mimicked caveolin deficiency due to a concomitant, massive decrease of caveolin protein levels.
source: CAVIN-1 KO phenotypically mimicked caveolin deficiency merely due to a concomitant, massive decrease of caveolin protein levels (Hill et al., 2008; Liu and Pilch, 2008; Liu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hill et al., 2008; Liu and Pilch, 2008; Liu et al., 2008.

claim: RNAi against syndapin II led to a reduction of deeply invaginated caveolae without affecting the presence of endogenous cav1 at the plasma membrane of NIH3T3 cells.
source: RNAi against the F-BAR protein syndapin II led to a reduction of deeply invaginated caveolae without affecting the presence of endogenous cav1 at the plasma membrane of NIH3T3 cells (Koch et al., 2012) and to increased levels of overexpressed cav1 in the TIRF-zone of HeLa cells (Hansen et al., 2011), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Koch et al., 2012.

claim: RNAi against syndapin II led to increased levels of overexpressed cav1 in the TIRF-zone of HeLa cells.
source: RNAi against the F-BAR protein syndapin II led to a reduction of deeply invaginated caveolae without affecting the presence of endogenous cav1 at the plasma membrane of NIH3T3 cells (Koch et al., 2012) and to increased levels of overexpressed cav1 in the TIRF-zone of HeLa cells (Hansen et al., 2011), respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hansen et al., 2011.

claim: Syndapin III KO mice were viable, developed without any obvious impairments and were fertile.
source: Syndapin III KO mice were viable, developed without any obvious impairments and were fertile.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse colony.

claim: Litter of heterozygous syndapin III KO mice showed normal Mendelian and gender distributions.
source: Litter of heterozygous syndapin III KO mice showed normal Mendelian and gender distributions (Figure 1l).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1l.

claim: Syndapin III is enriched at the cav3-positive plasma membranes in sections of skeletal muscles.
source: Analyses of WT samples showed that syndapin III is enriched at the cav3-positive plasma membranes in sections of skeletal muscles (Figure 1p–r).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1p-r.

claim: Colocalization of syndapin III and cav3 was very high at the plasma membrane (Pearson correlation coefficient 0.55 ± 0.01) and not existing at all in intracellular areas (Pearson correlation coefficient 0.08 ± 0.01).
source: Colocalization in transversal tissue sections hereby was very high at the plasma membrane (Pearson correlation coefficient 0.55 ± 0.01) and not existing at all in intracellular areas (Pearson correlation coefficient 0.08 ± 0.01), respectively (Figure 1q).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative colocalization analyses shown in Figure 1q.

claim: Cardiomyocytes from newborn WT pups showed plasma membrane areas with high frequencies of profiles resembling those of caveolae.
source: Cardiomyocytes from newborn WT pups showed plasma membrane areas with high frequencies of profiles resembling those of caveolae (Figure 2a,a').
evidence: This is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 2a,a'.

claim: The plasma membranes of cardiomyocytes from syndapin III KO mice largely lacked deeply invaginated structures.
source: In contrast, the plasma membranes of cardiomyocytes from syndapin III KO mice largely lacked deeply invaginated structures (Figure 2b,b').
evidence: This is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 2b,b'.

claim: WT membranes showed about 2 caveolae/µm membrane stretch.
source: WT membranes showed about 2 caveolae/µm membrane stretch.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Syndapin III KO mice displayed 0.29 caveolae/µm, that is only 15% of WT.
source: Syndapin III KO mice displayed 0.29 caveolae/µm, that is only 15% of WT (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses of TEM images shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The expression levels of syndapin II remained unchanged in both heart and skeletal muscles upon syndapin III KO.
source: Quantitative western blotting analyses of syndapin II showed that also the expression levels of the more ubiquitously expressed syndapin family member, syndapin II (Qualmann and Kelly, 2000), remained unchanged in both heart and skeletal muscles (Figure 2e–h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative western blot data shown in Figure 2e-h.

claim: Of all syndapin III immunolabels, 77% were associated with membrane invaginations.
source: Anti-syndapin III immunolabeling was largely associated with areas of membrane curvature (Figure 3a,b). Of all syndapin III immunolabels, 77% were associated with membrane invaginations (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses of freeze-fracture EM data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The anti-cav3 labeling yielded in average 7.1 anti-cav3 labels/deeply invaginated caveola.
source: The immunolabelings of the freeze-fractured samples yielded high anti-cav3 labeling densities of in average 7.1 anti-cav3 labels/deeply invaginated caveola.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses of immunogold labeling in freeze-fracture EM.

claim: 58% of all observed invaginations were anti-syndapin III-labeled caveolae-like invaginations (deep and shallow) with 35% being colabeled for cav3 and syndapin III.
source: Quantitative analyses showed that 58% of all observed invaginations were anti-syndapin III-labeled caveolae-like invaginations (deep and shallow) with 35% being colabeled for cav3 and syndapin III (Figure 3j).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 3j.

claim: The density of shallow cav3-immunopositive indentations was unchanged upon syndapin III KO.
source: Strikingly, scoring extended membrane areas (64.8 µm2 in total) unveiled that whereas the density of shallow cav3-immunopositive indentations was unchanged, specifically the density of cav3-marked, deep invaginations – that is classical caveolae - was severely reduced in syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes when compared to cardiomyocytes prepared from WT mice (Figure 3i,i',k,l; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 3l.

claim: The density of cav3-marked, deep invaginations was severely reduced in syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes when compared to WT.
source: Strikingly, scoring extended membrane areas (64.8 µm2 in total) unveiled that whereas the density of shallow cav3-immunopositive indentations was unchanged, specifically the density of cav3-marked, deep invaginations – that is classical caveolae - was severely reduced in syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes when compared to cardiomyocytes prepared from WT mice (Figure 3i,i',k,l; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 3k.

claim: The overall anti-cav3 immunolabeling density at the plasma membrane of WT and syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes remained about the same.
source: The overall anti-cav3 immunolabeling density at the plasma membrane of WT and syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes remained about the same (Figure 3o).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 3o.

claim: The density of the cav3 labeling within ROIs of 150 nm diameter covering caveolae as well as cav3 clusters at shallow or flat membranes was unchanged in syndapin III KO cells when compared to WT cells.
source: The density of the cav3 labeling within ROIs of 150 nm diameter covering caveolae as well as cav3 clusters at shallow or flat membranes also was unchanged in syndapin III KO cells when compared to WT cells (Figure 3p).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 3p.

claim: Syndapin III specifically associates with cav3-coated caveolae and is not found at cav1-coated caveolae from non-muscle cells.
source: Thus, syndapin III specifically associates with cav3-coated caveolae and is not found at cav1-coated caveolae from non-muscle cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and EM data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cav1-coated caveolae found in the primary cell cultures were unaffected by syndapin III KO, that is were invaginated normally.
source: Consistently, cav1-coated caveolae found in the primary cell cultures were unaffected by syndapin III KO, that is were invaginated normally (Figure 3—figure supplement 3f).
evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3f.

claim: The expression levels of CAVIN-1 were unchanged in both hearts and skeletal muscles of syndapin III KO mice.
source: Quantitative western blot analyses, however, demonstrated that the expression levels of CAVIN-1 were unchanged in both hearts and skeletal muscles of syndapin III KO mice (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative western blot data shown in Figure 4a,b.

claim: The expression of cav1, CAVIN-2, CAVIN-3, and CAVIN-4 was unchanged upon syndapin III KO.
source: Also, the expression of the other CAVIN proteins (Cheng et al., 2015) as well as that of the non-muscle caveolin, cav1, was unchanged (Figure 4c–f).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative western blot data shown in Figure 4c-f.

claim: CAVIN-1's membrane association and its ability to form clusters is not impaired in syndapin III KO cells.
source: Surprisingly, CAVIN-1's membrane association, its ability to form clusters and its colocalization with cav3 seemed not to be impaired upon syndapin III KO (Figure 4h; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunogold labeling data shown in Figure 4h and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: CAVIN-1 levels at the plasma membrane were not reduced upon syndapin III KO and/or the presence of predominantly flat cav3 clusters; instead, the CAVIN-1 density at the plasma membrane moderately increased by about 30%.
source: However, quantitative evaluations of our ultra-high-resolution imaging experiments clearly confirmed that CAVIN-1 levels at the plasma membrane were not reduced upon syndapin III KO and/or the presence of predominantly flat cav3 clusters caused by the loss of syndapin III. Instead, the CAVIN-1 density at the plasma membrane even moderately increased by about 30% (Figure 4i).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 4i.

claim: The CAVIN-1 density within CAVIN-1 clusters rose accordingly upon syndapin III KO.
source: The CAVIN-1 density within CAVIN-1 clusters rose accordingly (Figure 4j).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 4j.

claim: The density of CAVIN-1 clusters found was increased upon syndapin III KO.
source: Since also the density of CAVIN-1 clusters found was increased (Figure 4k), these increases of CAVIN-1 in clusters at syndapin III KO plasma membranes of cardiomyocytes obviously came at the expense of the disperse labeling.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 4k.

claim: Even a combination of cav3 and CAVIN-1 residing at the plasma membrane is insufficient for caveolar invagination, if syndapin III is lacking.
source: Our observations also unveiled that even a combination of cav3 and CAVIN-1 residing at the plasma membrane is insufficient for caveolar invagination, if syndapin III is lacking.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both cav3 and CAVIN-1 are present at the plasma membrane in syndapin III KO cells, yet caveolar invaginations are severely impaired.

claim: Both tagged and untagged full-length syndapin III formed tubules with an average diameter of about 80 nm.
source: Both tagged and untagged full-length syndapin III formed tubules with an average diameter of about 80 nm (Figure 5a–e).
evidence: This is supported by freeze-fracture/TEM and cryo-TEM data shown in Figure 5a-e.

claim: The observed diameter range of 75–90 nm for syndapin III-induced tubules corresponded very well to the membrane topologies that were immuno-positive for syndapin III in vivo.
source: The observed diameter range of 75–90 nm corresponded very well to the membrane topologies that were immuno-positive for syndapin III in vivo. Cav3-caveolae had diameters of 60–80 nm (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of in vitro tubule measurements with in vivo caveolar measurements.

claim: Syndapin III was not found at the lateral walls or at the bottom of caveolar invaginations but was restricted to areas of membrane curvature transition from the caveolar invagination to the continuum of the plasma membrane.
source: EM tomograms and 3D-segmentations of membrane topology in combination with the 3D-detection of immunogold labels indeed demonstrated that syndapin III was not found at the lateral walls or at the bottom of caveolar invaginations but was restricted to areas of membrane curvature transition from the caveolar invagination to the continuum of the plasma membrane (Figure 5f–h; Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by EM tomography and 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 5f-h and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: The syndapin III F-BAR-domain interacts with cav3 coats.
source: Coprecipitations from heart lysates confirmed that the syndapin III F-BAR-domain interacts with cav3 coats.
evidence: This is supported by coprecipitation data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The interactions between syndapin III F-BAR domain and cav3 were rather weak.
source: Interestingly, similar to the caveolin coat component CAVIN-1 showing only weak – if any – interactions with caveolin (Hill et al., 2008; Liu and Pilch, 2008; Mohan et al., 2015), the interactions were rather weak and therefore suggested that syndapin III may not represent a general and integral part of cav3 coats (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by coprecipitation data shown in Figure 6a and comparison with literature on CAVIN-1.

claim: Overexpression of the F-BAR-domain of syndapin III led to colocalization of endogenous cav3 at F-BAR-enriched sites at the plasma membrane of primary cardiomyocytes.
source: However, similar to syndapin II and cav1 in some cell lines (Koch et al., 2012; Senju et al., 2011), overexpression of the F-BAR-domain of syndapin III led to colocalization of endogenous cav3 at F-BAR-enriched sites at the plasma membrane of primary cardiomyocytes (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6b,c.

claim: Cav3 and syndapin III both floated together in TritonX-100-resistant membrane preparations.
source: Preparations of TritonX-100-resistant membranes (DRMs) demonstrated that cav3 and syndapin III both floated together (Figure 6d,e).
evidence: This is supported by DRM fractionation data shown in Figure 6d,e.

claim: Cav3 showed an altered distribution upon syndapin III KO in DRM preparations.
source: Interestingly, cav3 showed an altered distribution upon syndapin III KO (Figure 6f–i; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by DRM fractionation data shown in Figure 6f-i and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In WT heart samples, syndapin III and cav3 floated to fraction F4+F5.
source: In WT heart samples, syndapin III and cav3 floated to fraction F4+F5.
evidence: This is supported by DRM fractionation data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Syndapin III KO fractions F4+F5 were devoid of cav3 but cav3 mainly floated to fractions F6+F7 in heart.
source: Syndapin III KO fractions F4+F5 were devoid of cav3 but cav3 mainly floated to fractions F6+F7 (Figure 6d,f,h; Figure 6—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is supported by DRM fractionation data shown in Figure 6f,h and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: Related shifts of cav3 toward higher densities were observed for preparations from syndapin III KO skeletal muscles.
source: Related shifts of cav3 toward higher densities were observed for preparations from syndapin III KO skeletal muscles (Figure 6e,g,i; Figure 6—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is supported by DRM fractionation data shown in Figure 6e,g,i and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: Relative phosphoERK1/2 levels were not altered upon syndapin III KO.
source: Relative phosphoERK1/2 levels were not altered upon syndapin III KO (Figure 7a,b).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 7a,b.

claim: No localization defects of dystrophin and β-dystroglycan could be detected in sections of skeletal muscles from syndapin III KO mice.
source: No localization defects of dystrophin and β-dystroglycan could be detected in sections of skeletal muscles from syndapin III KO mice (Figure 7c–f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7c-f.

claim: Dystrophin and β-dystroglycan expression levels were unaltered upon syndapin III KO in both heart and skeletal muscle.
source: Also dystrophin and β-dystroglycan expression levels were unaltered upon syndapin III KO in both heart and skeletal muscle (Figure 7g–j).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative immunoblot data shown in Figure 7g-j.

claim: The immediate cell response to increased membrane tensions induced by hypoosmotic conditions is a reduction of caveolar invaginations in NIH3T3 cells.
source: Our TEM analyses of freeze-fractured NIH3T3 cells, which we labeled for cav1 (in average 13.9 anti-cav1 labels/caveola (iso)), confirm that the immediate cell response to increased membrane tensions induced by hypoosmotic conditions is a reduction of caveolar invaginations (Figure 8—figure supplement 1a–d).
evidence: This is supported by freeze-fracture EM data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1a-d.

claim: In NIH3T3 cells, cav1 remained at the plasma membrane upon hypoosmotic stress.
source: In NIH3T3 cells, cav1 hereby remained at the plasma membrane (Figure 8—figure supplement 1e–h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1e-h.

claim: The induced mechanical stress dramatically reduced deeply invaginated, cav3-positive structures (−75%) in primary mouse cardiomyocytes.
source: The induced mechanical stress dramatically reduced deeply invaginated, cav3-positive structures (−75%) (Figure 8a–d).
evidence: This is supported by freeze-fracture EM data shown in Figure 8a-d.

claim: The anti-cav3 labeling density at the plasma membrane remained constant upon hypoosmotic flattening of caveolae in primary mouse cardiomyocytes.
source: Again, the anti-cav3 labeling density at the plasma membrane remained constant upon hypoosmotic flattening of caveolae (Figure 8e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 8e.

claim: WT cardiomyocytes were able to fully cope with moderate hypoosmotic stress (hypo30) and were only moderately affected by stronger hypoosmotic stress (hypo15).
source: WT cells were able to fully cope with moderate stress (hypo30) and were only moderately affected by stronger hypoosmotic stress (hypo15) (Figure 8i–k,o).
evidence: This is supported by Trypan Blue assay data shown in Figure 8i-k,o.

claim: Syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes showed a significantly higher vulnerability under both moderate and stronger hypoosmotic stress conditions.
source: In contrast, syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes showed a significantly higher vulnerability under both conditions (Figure 8l–o).
evidence: This is supported by Trypan Blue assay data shown in Figure 8l-o.

claim: Syndapin III KO mice did not show hypertrophic cardiac myocytes.
source: Syndapin III KO mice were viable and heart sections of juvenile mice did not show any hypertrophic cardiac myocytes (Figure 9a–c).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 9a-c.

claim: Heart/body weight ratios were unaltered in syndapin III KO mice.
source: Heart weights (data not shown separately) and heart/body weight ratios were unaltered (Figure 9d,e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 9d,e.

claim: Left ventricle wall thickness did not differ from WT in syndapin III KO mice.
source: Left ventricle wall thickness also did not differ from WT (Figure 9f–h)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 9f-h.

claim: At >64 weeks of age, sections of syndapin III KO hearts did not show signs of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy or necrosis.
source: Even at >64 weeks of age, sections of syndapin III KO hearts did not show signs of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy or necrosis.
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 9i-l.

claim: Physical exercise-induced necrosis was not detectable in syndapin III KO hearts.
source: Physical exercise-induced necrosis was not detectable either (Figure 9i–l).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 9i-l.

claim: In heart tissue, the formation of caveolae is impaired upon syndapin III KO.
source: Our analyses of freeze-fractured and immunolabeled syndapin III KO hearts clearly demonstrated that, also in the tissue context, caveolar invagination was severely impaired (Figure 9m,n).
evidence: This is supported by freeze-fracture EM data shown in Figure 9m,n.

claim: Upon syndapin III KO, only 11.7% of the caveolae found in WT heart tissue remained.
source: Quantitative analyses showed that the effects even were slightly stronger than in dissociated cells. Upon syndapin III KO, only 11.7% of the caveolae found in WT remained.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 9o.

claim: The density of the shallow, cav3-positive indentations was significantly decreased in syndapin III KO hearts.
source: Even the density of the shallow, cav3-positive indentations was significantly decreased in syndapin III KO hearts (Figure 9o,p).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 9p.

claim: The anti-cav3 labeling density at membranes of freeze-fractured syndapin III KO hearts in total remained unchanged.
source: Consistent with the observations in dissociated cells, the anti-cav3 labeling density at membranes of freeze-fractured syndapin III KO hearts in total remained unchanged (Figure 9q).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 9q.

claim: The unchanged presence of cav3 at the membrane was in line with unchanged cav3 levels in TritonX-100-resistant membrane fractions from heart.
source: The unchanged presence of cav3 at the membrane was in line with unchanged cav3 levels in TritonX-100-resistant membrane fractions from heart observed by quantitative western blotting (Figure 9r).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative western blot data shown in Figure 9r.

claim: Cav3 labeling at deep and shallowly invaginated caveolar structures was strongly decreased in syndapin III KO hearts.
source: In accordance with the reduced densities of caveolae and cav3-positive indentations, cav3 labeling at deep and shallowly invaginated caveolar structures was strongly decreased (Figure 9s,t).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 9s,t.

claim: A significant portion of the caveolae found in muscle tissues were immunopositive for syndapin III.
source: A significant portion of the caveolae found in muscle tissues were immunopositive for syndapin III (Figure 10c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 10c.

claim: 32% of all cav3 spheres in skeletal muscle were positive for syndapin III.
source: 3D rendering of confocal image stacks of longitudinally cut muscle fibers showed that 32% of all cav3 spheres were positive for syndapin III (Figure 10m,n).
evidence: This is supported by 3D rendering analyses shown in Figure 10m,n.

claim: The density of deeply invaginated caveolae was dramatically reduced upon syndapin III KO in skeletal muscle.
source: Yet, despite the fact that syndapin III is only found at a (albeit significant) fraction of caveolae at a given time and despite the undisturbed presence of cav3 at the plasma membrane, the density of deeply invaginated caveolae was dramatically reduced upon syndapin III KO (Figure 10o).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 10o.

claim: The shallow, cav3-positive indentations were strongly reduced albeit not as dramatically as the deeply invaginated caveolae in syndapin III KO skeletal muscle.
source: Also the shallow, cav3-positive indentations were strongly reduced albeit not as dramatically as the deeply invaginated caveolae (Figure 10o,p).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 10o,p.

claim: Freeze-fractured skeletal muscles from syndapin III KO mice still showed about 70% of the cav3 cluster density observed in WT muscles.
source: Instead, freeze-fractured skeletal muscles from syndapin III KO mice still showed about 70% of the cav3 cluster density observed in WT muscles (Figure 10s)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 10s.

claim: The cav3 density within the persisting cav3 cluster ROIs only showed a minor reduction (−7%) in syndapin III KO skeletal muscle.
source: and the cav3 density within the persisting cav3 cluster ROIs only showed a minor reduction (−7%; Figure 10t).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 10t.

claim: Syndapin III KO mice displayed a higher frequency of detached nuclei upon training.
source: Whereas no clear signs of cellular damage or disintegration were observed by H&E staining under untrained conditions (a,b), syndapin III KO mice displayed a higher frequency of detached nuclei upon training (c), arrows).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 11c and quantitative analyses in Figure 11g,h.

claim: Acidic phosphatase stainings clearly demonstrate necrotic events in trained syndapin III KO muscles.
source: (e,f) Acidic phosphatase stainings clearly demonstrate necrotic events (asterisks in c) and e).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 11e.

claim: Detached nuclei were about three times more frequent in trained syndapin III KO muscles compared to WT.
source: Whereas WT muscles did not show any increase in the frequency of detached nuclei upon training (about 1% in murine musculus gastrocnemius), detached nuclei were about three times more frequent in trained syndapin III KO muscles (Figure 11g,h).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 11g,h.

claim: Untrained syndapin III KO muscles showed an expansion of the caliber spectrum.
source: Untrained syndapin III KO muscles showed an expansion of the caliber spectrum.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 11i.

claim: Weakly established fibers showed a notable abundance in syndapin III KO mice.
source: Especially weakly established fibers showed a notable abundance in syndapin III KO mice (Figure 11i,k).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 11i,k.

claim: The increased abundance of fibers with only small cross-sections in syndapin III KO mice was compensated for by hypertrophy upon training.
source: Interestingly, this increased abundance of fibers with only small cross-sections in syndapin III KO mice was compensated for by hypertrophy upon training (Figure 11i–l).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analyses shown in Figure 11i-l.

claim: Training-induced hypertrophy of syndapin III KO muscles was accompanied with increased rates of detached nuclei and of inflammation and necrosis.
source: This training-induced hypertrophy of syndapin III KO muscles, however, obviously was accompanied with increased rates of detached nuclei (Figure 11h) and of inflammation and necrosis (Figure 11e).
evidence: This is supported by histological and quantitative data shown in Figure 11e,h.

claim: Syndapin III plays a crucial role in organizing caveolar coats and associated lipid environments.
source: Together, these data strongly suggest that syndapin III plays a critical role in organizing caveolar coats and associated lipid environments.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing altered distribution of cav3 in DRM fractions upon syndapin III KO.

claim: Syndapin III is important specifically for invagination of cav3-coated caveolae found in muscle cells.
source: It can therefore be firmly concluded that syndapin III is important specifically for invagination of cav3-coated caveolae found in muscle cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cav1-coated caveolae are unaffected by syndapin III KO while cav3-coated caveolae are severely impaired.

claim: CAVIN-1 forms a flexible, net-like protein mesh around caveolin complexes.
source: CAVIN-1, a caveolae-associated protein, which forms a flexible, net-like protein mesh around caveolin complexes (Stoeber et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Stoeber et al., 2016.

claim: Bacterial reconstitutions suggested that caveolins were sufficient for caveolar invagination.
source: Bacterial reconstitutions, furthermore, suggested that caveolins also were sufficient for caveolar invagination (Walser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Walser et al., 2012.

claim: Syndapins associate with phosphatidylserine using their F-BAR-domains.
source: Third, syndapins associate with phosphatidylserine using their F-BAR-domains (Qualmann et al., 2011; Itoh et al., 2005; Dharmalingam et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Qualmann et al., 2011; Itoh et al., 2005; Dharmalingam et al., 2009.

claim: Caveolar microdomains are enriched for phosphatidylserine.
source: and caveolar microdomains are enriched for phosphatidylserine (Fairn et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fairn et al., 2011.

claim: Caveolae morphology and density at the plasma membrane of rat myofibers were unchanged upon different modes of contractile activity as well as upon myofiber stretching within normal myofiber limits but were greatly reduced by the more severe mechanical forces occurring during tearing of myofibers.
source: Interestingly, caveolae morphology and density at the plasma membrane of rat myofibers were found to be unchanged upon different modes of contractile activity as well as upon myofiber stretching within normal myofiber limits but were greatly reduced by the more severe mechanical forces occurring during tearing of myofibers (Poulos et al., 1986; Dulhunty and Franzini-Armstrong, 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Poulos et al., 1986 and Dulhunty and Franzini-Armstrong, 1975.

claim: Muscular caveolar invaginations are largely dispensable for life.
source: Taken together, it seems that muscular caveolar invaginations are largely dispensable for life. This is in line with the viability of cav3 KO mice (Hagiwara et al., 2000; Galbiati et al., 2001; Woodman et al., 2002).
evidence: This is inferred from the viability of syndapin III KO mice and supported by citations to cav3 KO mouse studies.

claim: Muscular caveolae help to preserve muscle cells from abrupt tear forces.
source: Yet, our studies unveil that muscular caveolae help to preserve muscle cells from the abrupt tear forces.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that syndapin III KO muscles show pathology upon physical exercise.

claim: When caveolae as membrane tension compensators are impaired, physical exercise-inducible hypertrophy is counterproductive to compensate the weakness of muscle fibers.
source: Our data thereby shed light on the exact cellular functions impaired in caveolinopathies and strongly suggest that, when caveolae as membrane tension compensators are impaired, physical exercise-inducible hypertrophy is counterproductive to compensate the weakness of muscle fibers.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that trained syndapin III KO muscles show hypertrophy accompanied by increased necrosis and detached nuclei.
